ambiguity: Option<Params> fold (arc_fitting, segment_merge, dogbone, lead_in_out, link_moves; config.rs:910-918) versus flat bool + value fields (feed_optimization, feed_max_rate, feed_ramp_rate and optimize_rapid_order; config.rs:919-928). The struct doc at :883-895 says the Option form is CUT-13's fix, but the comment at :921-925 says the flat shape was kept for feed_optimization because another session owns a reader. Both are live in the same struct.

Dressup vs op-specific stage: the always-on air-cut filter (DressupStage::AIR_CUT_FILTER, dressup_apply.rs:~225, run unconditionally when prior stock, cutter and kinematics exist; no config field) versus a configured stage. A stage with no DressupConfig field never reaches FIELD_DEFS, GUI, MCP or CLI. A reader could copy either.

Two rapid-order slots (barriered and unbarriered; both DressupStage::RAPID_ORDER) and the entry slot (RAMP_ENTRY/HELIX_ENTRY/PLUNGE_ENTRY with the same debug_key 'entry_style') show that a stage may reuse a key. The test at dressup_span_invariants.rs:~525 says label must be distinct and key need not be. Unclear which rule a new stage should follow.

Where in the GUI: the Linking tab (draw_linking_params, linking_dressup.rs:~310, entry, links, rapid order, 'Advanced' feed optimisation) versus the Dressup tab (draw_dressup_params, :621, 'Path Quality': arc fitting, dogbone). The doc comment at :308-311 says edge work stays in draw_dressup_params. A path-quality post-processor fits either, and segment_merge, the newest and closest sibling, is in neither.

Applied by the dressup pipeline vs applied by the planner: segment_merge is skipped in the pipeline and run in the planner for some ops (dressup_apply.rs:813-840 with `by_planner`). A dressup that post-processes a toolpath could follow the plain arc-fit pattern (:781) or the segment-merge pattern with the planner twin. The doc does not say which a new dressup is.

Closest example to copy: arc_fitting (full GUI, role defaults, MCP, FIELD_DEFS, multitool override at session/multitool.rs:937-942) versus segment_merge (newest, has the serde-default, planner and capability coupling, but no GUI). Neither is a complete template on its own.
